questions.question: What was the day of the week on 26 January 2018?
questions.solution:
​The given date is **26 January 2018**.

We break down the time until this date: **2017 full years** + **26 days** of 2018.

Odd days in 2000 years = **0**.

Odd days in the remaining 17 years (from 2001 to 2017):

Number of **leap years** in 17 years = 17 ÷ 4 = **4** (2004, 2008, 2012, 2016)

Number of **ordinary years** = 17 − 4 = **13**

Total odd days = (4 × 2) + (13 × 1) = 8 + 13 = 21 days

21 ÷ 7 = 3 weeks and **0 odd days**.

Days in the year 2018 until 26 January:

Total days = 26

26 ÷ 7 = 3 weeks and **5 odd days**.

Total odd days = 0 + 0 + 5 = **5 odd days**.

Based on the day code table, 5 corresponds to **Friday**.

Hence, the day of the week on **26 January 2018** was **Friday**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Using the calendar formula: [Date + Month Code + Century Code + Year + (Year ÷ 4)] ÷ 7

Where:

Date = 26

**Month Code** (January for non-leap year) = 0

**Century Code** (2000) = 6

Year (last 2 digits) = 18

Leap Year part (18 ÷ 4) = 4

Sum = 26 + 0 + 6 + 18 + 4 = 54

Now, divide the sum by 7 to find the remainder: 54 ÷ 7 = 7 remainder **5**.

Remainder 5 represents **Friday**.

Hence, the correct answer is **Friday**.

questions.question: Which fundamental right was removed from the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Property**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution of India** originally recognized **seven fundamental rights** under **Part III**, which serves as the foundational charter of civil liberties in the country.
 
• The **Right to Property** was initially protected under two specific provisions: **Article 19(1)(f)**, which guaranteed the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property, and **Article 31**, which protected citizens against the compulsory acquisition of their property.
 
• During the tenure of the **Janata Party government**, the **44th Amendment Act, 1978** was passed, which formally removed the **Right to Property** from the list of fundamental rights.
 
• This legislative change was primarily driven by the need to implement **land reforms** and facilitate **socialist redistribution of resources** without the legal bottlenecks created by fundamental right challenges in the courts.
 
• Following the amendment, the right was transitioned to **Part XII** of the Constitution as **Article 300A**, where it currently exists as a **legal right** or **constitutional right**.
 
• As a result of this reclassification, the **Right to Property** is no longer enforceable through the **writ jurisdiction** of the **Supreme Court** under **Article 32**, although it still mandates that no person can be deprived of property except by **authority of law**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Education**:

 
 
• It was established as a fundamental right through the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**.
 
• Under **Article 21A**, the state must provide free and compulsory education to all children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
 
 
• **Right to Equality**:
 
 
• It is encapsulated within **Articles 14 to 18** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This includes equality before the law (**Article 14**) and the abolition of **untouchability** (**Article 17**).
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion**:
 
 
• These rights are detailed under **Articles 25 to 28**.
 
• They guarantee the freedom of conscience and the right to freely **profess, practice, and propagate** any religion.

__
 
• **Article 30** of the **Indian Constitution** is specifically designed to protect the interests of **religious** and **linguistic minorities**, granting them the right to **establish** and **administer** educational institutions of their choice.
 
• Under **Article 30(1)**, all minorities have the fundamental right to manage their institutions, which includes choosing their **governing bodies**, appointing qualified staff, and admitting students while maintaining their unique **cultural** or **religious** identity.
 
• The **44th Amendment Act, 1978**, introduced **Article 30(1A)**, which mandates that the State must provide appropriate **compensation** if it compulsorily acquires the property of a minority educational institution, ensuring that the right to establish such institutions is not hindered.
 
• **Article 30(2)** prohibits the State from **discriminating** against any educational institution in terms of providing **financial aid** or recognition solely because it is under the management of a religious or linguistic minority.
 
• While these rights are absolute in terms of **management**, they are subject to reasonable state regulations regarding **academic standards**, health, sanitation, and **public order** to ensure educational excellence.

• Guarantees the **freedom of conscience** and the right to freely **profess**, **practice**, and **propagate** religion.
 
• It is subject to **public order**, **morality**, and **health**, and allows the State to regulate secular activities associated with religious practice.
 
 
 
• **Article 28**:
 
 
• Provides freedom regarding attendance at **religious instruction** or **worship** in certain educational institutions.
 
• It distinguishes between institutions **wholly maintained by the State** (where religious instruction is prohibited) and those aided by the State.
 
 
 
• **Article 29**:
 
 
• Focuses on the **protection of interests** of any section of citizens residing in India who have a distinct **language**, **script**, or **culture**.

questions.question: Which instrument is most commonly used in Bhangra music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dhol** is a large, double-sided barrel drum that serves as the essential rhythmic heartbeat of **Bhangra music** and the associated folk dance from **Punjab**.
 
• Historically, the instrument played a crucial role in **agrarian Punjabi society**, used to celebrate the **Vaisakhi festival** and to signal the successful completion of the harvest.
 
• It is played using two wooden sticks: a thick, curved stick called the **dagga** for the bass side and a thin bamboo stick called the **tilli** for the treble side.
 
• The **Dhol** provides the signature **chaal rhythm**, a syncopated 8-beat pattern that defines the high-energy nature of **Bhangra** performances.
 
• While other percussion instruments exist in Punjabi folk, the **Dhol** is the most iconic and loud, making it suitable for large outdoor gatherings and festive processions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tabla**:

 
 
• A pair of hand drums consisting of the **Dayan** (right) and **Bayan** (left).
 
• It is the primary percussion instrument for **Hindustani Classical music** and is used for intricate rhythmic patterns rather than the loud, booming beats required for **Bhangra**.
 
 
 
• **Sitar**:
 
 
• A plucked string instrument belonging to the **lute family**, featuring sympathetic strings and a long hollow neck.
 
• It is a staple of **Indian classical music** and is generally not used as a lead instrument in traditional **Bhangra** folk compositions.
 
 
 
• **Violin**:
 
 
• A **bowed chordophone** that was adapted into the Indian musical tradition.
 
• It is particularly prominent in **Carnatic music** of South India, though it occasionally appears in modern fusion versions of **Bhangra**.

questions.question: Which method is commonly used to correct a cataract in the human eye?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surgery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **cataract** is a medical condition involving the **opacification** or clouding of the eye's **natural crystalline lens**, which is normally clear to allow light to focus on the **retina**.
 
• The condition is primarily caused by the aggregation of **crystallin proteins** within the lens due to **oxidative stress**, **aging**, or **UV radiation**, leading to blurred vision and eventual blindness if left untreated.
 
• **Surgery** is the only definitive corrective method; it involves the extraction of the **cloudy lens** and the implantation of a clear, artificial **Intraocular Lens (IOL)**.
 
• The most common surgical technique is **Phacoemulsification**, where an **ultrasonic probe** vibrates at high frequencies (approx. **40,000 Hz**) to emulsify the hardened lens for removal through a micro-incision.
 
• Clinical data suggests that **cataract surgery** has a success rate exceeding **95 percent**, making it one of the most frequently performed and safest medical procedures globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Limitations of Non-Surgical Options**:

 
 
• **Glasses and Contacts**: These can improve **visual acuity** in the very early stages by correcting **refractive errors** caused by lens changes, but they cannot reverse the **protein clumping** in the lens.
 
• **Eye Drops**: While **lubricating drops** or **medicated drops** treat surface issues or **glaucoma**, no pharmacological agent is currently approved to dissolve a **cataract**.
 
 
 
• **Risk Factors and Prevention**:
 
 
• **Systemic Conditions**: Chronic diseases such as **Diabetes Mellitus** and **Hypertension** significantly increase the rate of **lens opacification**.
 
• **Environmental Factors**: Long-term exposure to **ultraviolet (UV) rays** and habits like **smoking** are major contributors to the early onset of **senile cataracts**.

questions.question: What is the maximum time allowed for an archer to shoot three arrows in target archery under official guidelines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 min**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Archery Federation** (formerly known as **FITA**) governs the official rules for target archery worldwide. Under these regulations, the standard time allotted for an archer to shoot an end of **three arrows** is exactly **2 minutes** (120 seconds).
 
• This timing rule is calculated based on a generous allowance of **40 seconds per arrow**. The 40-second-per-arrow benchmark is the international standard for individual indoor and outdoor target archery qualification rounds.
 
• The time limit is strictly monitored using **digital countdown clocks** and **acoustic signals** (whistles) to ensure that the competition proceeds efficiently and fairly for all participants.
 
• If an archer fails to release all three arrows within the **2-minute** window, any arrow shot after the expiration of time is penalized. Typically, the highest-scoring arrow of that end is forfeited and recorded as a miss (zero).
 
• This specific time frame applies to both the **Recurve** and **Compound** bow categories during standard ranking rounds in official tournaments like the **World Championships** and the **Olympic Games**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Visual and Acoustic Signaling:**

 
 
• **Green Light:** Indicates the start of the shooting period.
 
• **Amber (Yellow) Light:** This signal usually appears when only **30 seconds** remain in the 2-minute block, serving as a warning for the archer to complete their shots.
 
• **Red Light:** Indicates that the time has expired and no more arrows may be released.
 
• **Whistle Commands:** One blast of the whistle signals the start of shooting, while two blasts signal the archers to move to the shooting line.
 
 
 
• **Alternate Match Play:**
 
 
• In high-stakes **Match Play** (head-to-head eliminations), the time limit is often reduced to **20 seconds per arrow**. In these cases, archers shoot one arrow at a time alternately, which adds significant pressure to the timing and execution.
 
 
 
• **Six-Arrow Ends:**
 
 
• In some tournament formats, archers shoot ends of **six arrows**. In such scenarios, the time limit is doubled to **4 minutes** (240 seconds), maintaining the same ratio of 40 seconds per arrow.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adenosine triphosphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adenosine triphosphate (ATP)** is a complex organic chemical that provides energy to drive many processes in living cells, such as **muscle contraction**, **nerve impulse propagation**, and **chemical synthesis**.
 
• The molecular structure of ATP consists of a **nitrogenous base (adenine)**, a **pentose sugar (ribose)**, and a chain of **three phosphate groups** covalently bonded to the sugar.
 
• It is universally recognized as the **'energy currency'** of life because it captures chemical energy obtained from the **breakdown of food molecules** and releases it to fuel other cellular processes.
 
• Energy is stored within the **phosphoanhydride bonds** linking the phosphate groups; the **hydrolysis** of the terminal phosphate bond releases approximately **30.5 kJ/mol** of energy under standard conditions.
 
• Upon losing a phosphate group, ATP is converted into **Adenosine Diphosphate (ADP)**, which can then be recharged back into ATP during **cellular respiration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adenosine vs Adenine**:

 
 
• **Adenine** is a **purine nucleobase**, while **Adenosine** is a **nucleoside** formed when adenine is attached to a **ribose sugar** ring.
 
 
 
• **Phosphate Variations**:
 
 
• **ADP (Adenosine Diphosphate)** contains two phosphate groups and represents a partially discharged state of the energy carrier.
 
• **AMP (Adenosine Monophosphate)** contains a single phosphate group and is often involved in **cellular signaling** (e.g., cyclic AMP).
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**:
 
 
• Known as the **'powerhouse of the cell'**, these organelles are the primary sites where **oxidative phosphorylation** occurs to generate the bulk of the cell's ATP supply.

• The **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** is the third-generation launch vehicle developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, specifically designed to launch Indian Remote Sensing satellites into **Sun-synchronous orbits**.
 
• The **PSLV-D2** mission, conducted on **October 15, 1994**, was the second developmental flight and the first successful mission of the PSLV program, following the unsuccessful PSLV-D1 flight in 1993.
 
• The vehicle is famously known as a **four-stage** rocket, which alternates between **solid and liquid propulsion** systems to achieve high efficiency and precise orbital placement.
 
• The **first stage (PS1)** consists of an **S139 solid rocket motor** carrying 138 tonnes of **Hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene (HTPB)** propellant, supplemented by **six strap-on boosters** to provide initial liftoff thrust.
 
• The **second stage (PS2)** is powered by the **Vikas engine**, a liquid-propellant engine that utilizes **UH25** (a blend of **UDMH** and Hydrazine Hydrate) and **Nitrogen Tetroxide** as the oxidizer.
 
• The **third stage (PS3)** uses a high-performance **solid rocket motor** that provides the necessary thrust for the vehicle's journey through the upper atmosphere.
 
• The **fourth stage (PS4)**, the final stage, utilizes a **twin-engine liquid propulsion system** using **Monomethylhydrazine (MMH)** and **Mixed Oxides of Nitrogen (MON-3)**, allowing for the precise injection of the satellite into its target orbit.
 
• During the **PSLV-D2** mission, the vehicle successfully placed the **804 kg IRS-P2 satellite** into an 817 km **Polar Sun-synchronous orbit**.

• The **PSLV** earned the title 'Workhorse of ISRO' due to its consistent reliability in launching various national and international satellites.
 
• It was the vehicle used for India's first interplanetary mission, the **Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)**, and the first lunar probe, **Chandrayaan-1**.
 
• The **Vikas engine** used in the second stage was developed by the **Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC)** and was named after **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**, the father of the Indian space program.
 
• Standard variants of the PSLV include the **PSLV-G** (Generic), **PSLV-CA** (Core Alone), and **PSLV-XL**, differing primarily in the use and power of the strap-on boosters rather than the core stage count.

• In the sport of **Kabaddi**, a **bonus point** is a tactical scoring mechanism awarded to a raider for reaching the **bonus line** under specific defensive conditions.
 
• The **bonus line** only becomes active when the defending team (the catchers) has a minimum of **6 players** or a maximum of **7 players** present on the court.
 
• To successfully earn this point, the raider must cross the **bonus line** such that one foot is placed completely on the ground beyond the line, while the other foot (trailing foot) is lifted in the air, ensuring no contact with the ground behind or on the line.
 
• If the number of defenders on the mat is **5 or fewer**, the **bonus point** rule is suspended, meaning the raider cannot earn this extra point regardless of their foot placement.
 
• As per the regulations of the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)** and the **Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI)**, the bonus line is marked at **4.75 meters** from the **mid-line** in the men’s court and **4 meters** in the women’s court.

• This line is situated **3.75 meters** from the **mid-line**. A raider must cross this line with at least one foot to make a raid **valid**; failure to do so results in the raider being declared out.
 
 
 
• **Super Tackle**:
 
 
• A **Super Tackle** occurs when a raider is successfully caught by a defense consisting of **3 or fewer players**. In this case, the defending team earns **2 points** instead of the standard 1 point.
 
 
 
• **Lona**:
 
 
• A **Lona** is awarded when a team manages to put out the entire opposing team. The side achieving this receives **2 bonus points**, and the entire opposition is then revived to resume play.
 
 
 
• **Do-or-Die Raid**:
 
 
• If a team completes two consecutive **empty raids** (raids where no points are scored), the third raid is designated as a **Do-or-Die raid**, where the raider must score a point or they will be declared out.

questions.question: What is the Highest Common Factor of 0.42, 0.60 and 0.78?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the decimals into **integers** by multiplying by 100: 42, 60, and 78.

Calculate the **differences** between the numbers: 60 − 42 = 18 and 78 − 60 = 18.

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** must be a factor of 18. Factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.

The largest factor that divides 42, 60, and 78 is **6**.

Re-apply the decimal by dividing by 100: 6 ÷ 100 = 0.06.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.06.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Decimal numbers 0.42, 0.60, and 0.78.

**Formula Used:** HCF of decimals = (HCF of integers obtained by making decimal places equal) ÷ (10ⁿ), where n is the number of decimal places.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d779872eb0f8b98a8fbb4aa1f01adbea66ea41a888423d32364cc026fde8b6f7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Express decimals as fractions: 42/100, 60/100, 78/100

⇒ To find the **HCF**, we find the **prime factorization** of the numerators:

⇒ 42 = 2 × 3 × 7

⇒ 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 2² × 3 × 5

⇒ 78 = 2 × 3 × 13

⇒ Common factors are 2 and 3. So, HCF(42, 60, 78) = 2 × 3 = 6.

⇒ Applying the common denominator: 6 ÷ 100 = 0.06.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.06.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Fractions

HCF = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators). Ensure fractions are in their simplest form before applying the rule.

LCM of Decimals

Like HCF, first make the number of decimal places equal for all numbers, find the LCM as integers, and then place the decimal point accordingly.

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF × LCM.

questions.question: The speed of stream is 4 km/hr. A boat goes 120 km upstream and comes back to the starting point in 40 hours. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **round trip** (Upstream + Downstream), use the direct formula: **Total Time = [2 × D × u] ÷ [u² − v²]**

Where **D = 120 km**, **v = 4 km/hr**, and **Total Time = 40 hr**.

40 = [2 × 120 × u] ÷ [u² − 4²] ⇒ 40 = 240u ÷ (u² − 16)

1 = 6u ÷ (u² − 16) ⇒ u² − 6u − 16 = 0

Solving the quadratic equation, we get **u = 8** (Since speed cannot be negative).

**∴ The correct answer is 8 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed of Stream (v)** = 4 km/hr

**Distance (D)** = 120 km

**Total Time (T)** = 40 hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Upstream Speed = u − v | Downstream Speed = u + v

**Calculations:**

⇒ [120 ÷ (u − 4)] + [120 ÷ (u + 4)] = 40

⇒ 120 × [(u + 4) + (u − 4)] ÷ [(u − 4)(u + 4)] = 40

⇒ 120 × [2u] ÷ (u² − 16) = 40

⇒ 240u ÷ (u² − 16) = 40

⇒ 6u = u² − 16

⇒ u² − 6u − 16 = 0

⇒ u² − 8u + 2u − 16 = 0

⇒ u(u − 8) + 2(u − 8) = 0

⇒ (u − 8)(u + 2) = 0

⇒ u = 8 or u = −2

⇒ **Speed of boat in still water (u)** = 8 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 8 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water (u) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Current

Speed of Stream (v) = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

Average Speed = (Downstream Speed × Upstream Speed) ÷ Still Water Speed = (u² − v²) ÷ u.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A series of workshops for skill development is being organised by the team.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is in the **Active Voice** and utilizes the **Present Continuous Tense**. The structural formula for this tense is: **Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object**.

• To convert a **Present Continuous** sentence into **Passive Voice**, the object of the active sentence ('a series of workshops for skill development') is transitioned into the **subject** position.

• The **Passive Voice** construction for this tense follows the rule: **New Subject + is/am/are + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent**.

• The noun phrase **'a series'** serves as the head of the subject. In English grammar, **'a series of'** is treated as a **singular collective unit**, which requires the singular auxiliary verb **'is'** to maintain **Subject-Verb Agreement**.

• The inclusion of the word **'being'** is a critical grammatical requirement to indicate the **continuous or progressive aspect** of the action.

• The main verb 'organise' is converted into its **Past Participle** form, which is **'organised'**.

• Finally, the original subject 'the team' is added as the **agent** of the action, preceded by the preposition **'by'**. Therefore, the resulting sentence is the logically and grammatically correct passive transformation.

 **Additional Information__**

• Analysis of **Tense Variations** in Passive Voice:

• **Simple Present Passive:** This uses the structure 'is/am/are + V3'. Option 1 ('is organised') is incorrect because it fails to represent the **ongoing action** found in the original sentence.

• **Past Continuous Passive:** This uses 'was/were + being + V3'. Option 3 ('was being organised') is incorrect because it changes the **timeframe** of the action from present to past.

• **Present Perfect Passive:** This follows 'has/have + been + V3'. Option 4 ('has been organised') is incorrect as it describes a **completed action** rather than a continuous one.

• General Rules for **Voice Conversion**:

• The **Object** of the active sentence always becomes the **Subject** of the passive sentence.

• The **Passive Voice** always requires a form of the verb **'to be'** followed by the **Past Participle** of the main verb.

• The **tense** of the sentence must remain consistent during the transformation from active to passive voice.

</ul

"She explained me the instructions carefully."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **me**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the usage of the pronoun **me** directly after the verb **explained**.
 
• Certain verbs like **explain**, **describe**, **suggest**, and **mention** do not take an indirect object (the person) immediately after them without a preposition.
 
• The correct grammatical structure for the verb **explain** is **explain something to someone**.
 
• In the given sentence, the preposition **to** is missing before the person (**me**). Therefore, **me** is the incorrect part.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'She explained the instructions **to me** carefully.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **explained:** This is the correct past tense form of the verb used to describe the action.
 
• **the instructions:** This is the **direct object** of the sentence and is used correctly.
 
• **carefully:** This is an **adverb of manner** that correctly modifies the verb **explained**, indicating how the action was performed.
 
• Common mistake: Students often confuse **explain** with verbs like **tell** or **give** (e.g., 'He told me' is correct, but 'He explained me' is incorrect).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Pathogen**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **'a thing that causes illness'** refers to any biological agent, such as a **microorganism**, that produces a **disease** or sickness in its host. (बीमारी पैदा करने वाली चीज़)
 
 
• **Example: **Medical researchers are constantly looking for the specific **thing that causes illness** in patients with rare symptoms.
 
 
 
• **'Pathogen'** is the formal scientific term for a **bacterium**, **virus**, or other **microorganism** that can cause **disease**. It acts as an umbrella term for all biological causes of sickness. (रोगजनक)
 
 
• **Example: **The laboratory confirmed that the **pathogen** responsible for the outbreak was spread through contaminated water.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate **one-word substitute** for **'a thing that causes illness'** is **'pathogen'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Pathogen**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their **Hindi meanings** and example sentences:

 
• **Virus** (विषाणु): An extremely small infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of an organism.
 
 
• **Example: **The common cold is a respiratory **infection** caused by a **virus**.
 
 
 
• **Bacterium** (जीवाणु): A member of a large group of **unicellular microorganisms** which have cell walls but lack organelles; some are harmful while others are beneficial.
 
 
• **Example: **The doctor prescribed **antibiotics** to eliminate the harmful **bacterium** in the patient's system.
 
 
 
• **Germ** (रोगाणु): A general and informal term for any **microorganism**, especially one that causes **disease**.
 
 
• **Example: **You should always wash your hands after being in public places to protect yourself from **germs**.

सही उत्तर है- **__अपराध शैली विश्लेषण__**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **अपराध शैली विश्लेषण** (Modus Operandi Analysis) एक ऐसी प्रक्रिया है जिसमें एक अपराधी द्वारा अपराध को अंजाम देने के लिए अपनाई गई **विशिष्ट विधियों** और **तरीकों** का तुलनात्मक अध्ययन किया जाता है।
 
• जब कोई अपराधी बार-बार अपराध करता है, तो वह अक्सर एक ही तरह के **पैटर्न** या **कार्यप्रणाली** का उपयोग करता है, जिसे उसकी 'अपराध शैली' कहा जाता है।
 
• इस विश्लेषण के माध्यम से जांच एजेंसियां विभिन्न अपराधों के बीच **संबंध स्थापित** कर सकती हैं और अपराधी की पहचान करने में सफल होती हैं।
 
• इसमें अपराधी द्वारा उपयोग किए गए **हथियारों**, प्रवेश करने के तरीकों, और अपराध स्थल पर छोड़े गए विशिष्ट **चिह्नों** की तुलना की जाती है।

**__Key Points__**

**गद्यांश के अनुसार:**

__
 
• प्रशिक्षित नागरिक किसी भी आपदा या आपातकालीन स्थिति में **'प्रथम उत्तरदाता'** (First Responders) के रूप में कार्य करते हैं।

• गद्यांश स्पष्ट करता है कि प्रशिक्षित नागरिकों की उपस्थिति से घटना स्थल पर होने वाली **अफरा-तफरी** को नियंत्रित किया जा सकता है।
 
• इससे **पुलिस और सुरक्षा बलों** का काम काफी आसान हो जाता है क्योंकि उन्हें बुनियादी प्रबंधन के लिए अतिरिक्त संघर्ष नहीं करना पड़ता।
